key_insight: DiaLLM shows that language models can often understand dialectal English better than they can generate it, revealing a robustness-generation gap. The paper’s main contribution is a controlled setup to study and improve dialect adaptation across multiple model families and training strategies.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the mismatch between dialect understanding and dialect generation in large language models, especially their tendency to produce standard, US-leaning English even when dialectal input is understood.
method: Continual pretraining of three open-weight language model families on the International Corpus of English.
Comparison of implicit vs. explicit post-training paradigms for dialect adaptation.
Combination of each post-training paradigm with three different model alignment strategies to enable controlled analysis.
impact: For AI practitioners, this work provides a practical framework for evaluating and improving dialect-aware generation, not just comprehension. It is useful for building more linguistically inclusive systems that respond more naturally across English dialects.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing continual pretraining, post-training, and alignment stages.
Two-column comparison graphic: dialect understanding vs. dialect generation.
Matrix chart comparing model families across implicit/explicit training and alignment strategies.
Examples icon strip showing standard English vs. dialectal outputs.
paper_title: DiaLLM: An Investigation into the Robustness-Generation Gap in English Dialect Adaptation
paper_authors: Jordan Painter, Dipankar Srirag, Adarsh Kappiyath, Diptesh Kanojia, Aditya Joshi
